mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-rising periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims coinciding with a decline in wage growth signals labor market weakness that dampens consumer confidence and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by > 2% in a month while HOUST falls by > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to a baseline of stable labor conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in personal consumption expenditures relative to GDP during the prior quarter indicates strengthening underlying demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the observed PCE/GDP growth acceleration (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production followed by a rebound exceeding 2 percentage points in the subsequent month suggests supply-side constraints easing, which can trigger optimism about future capacity utilization and drive positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO shows a double bottom pattern with a closing gap > 2% in the following month
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in the 20-day window following the identified pattern (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the consumer price index exceeds 2% in a month of declining real yields, it indicates a misalignment between inflation expectations and current rates, which can produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 2% and real yield (10Y T-bill) monthly change < -0.5%
regime_hint: inflation expectations rising faster than yields
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during periods of aligned inflation and yields (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% without a corresponding rise in wage growth suggests a tight labor market that can fuel inflationary pressures and weigh on equity valuations, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls consecutively below 4.8% for 4 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain non-negative despite sustained unemployment declines (Rank IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales above seasonally adjusted expectations, especially when consumer confidence is also high, create a dual demand signal that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS (seasonally adjusted) > 105% of prior month's level and HOUST > 102% of prior month's level in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the dual positive demand indicators (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the ratio of new home construction to existing home sales exceeding 1.5x in a month signals an oversupply situation in the housing market, which can trigger a short-term pessimism about economic growth and produce negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST new home construction / existing home sales ratio > 1.5 for a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the trigger is absent in the prior month (p > 0.1).
